universal_lens: Codebase divergence quantified via SHA diff and commit count; liveness mismatch implies safety degradation through unverified behavior. UUID validation and intent-id fallback mechanisms in checkout flows exhibit a structural mismatch between client-side generation and server-side enforcement, necessitating conformal inference for robustness.

GSE situational reasoning maps checkout state transitions through {valid, invalid, fallback} regimes, applying deterministic automata to enforce {intent-id, token} consistency during subscription lifecycle.

primitives.name: Deployment Divergence Count
primitives.verbatim_quote: --## Headline finding **Production is running a 112-commit-old build, and three surfaces are serving premium content to anonymous visitors.** `/api/ops/public-surface-truth` reports `deployment_sha: b71f7e28569c9a263389c64362ca85d88482f5c8`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'n_{\\text{commits}}': '\\text{integer, number of commits since deployment}', 'S_{\\text{surface}}': '\\text{set of surfaces, } |S_{\\text{surface}}| = 3'}
primitives.assumptions: Production SHA is fixed; HEAD SHA is current; surfaces are discrete entities.

layer2.mapping: Each surface's rendered behavior maps to its SHA-based state under a fixed-time evolution model.
layer2.telemetry: SHA mismatch between HEAD and deployed instance.

layer2.mapping: Leak emerges from inconsistent enforcement of access control logic across surfaces.

primitives.name: Redeploy Priority Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: **The highest-value action available this week is a redeploy, not a code change.** It involves no gate change.

primitives.name: UUID Validation Mismatch

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'intentId': 'dimensionless string identifier', 'fallback': 'base36-encoded string', 'UUID': '128-bit universally unique identifier'}
primitives.assumptions: Client-side UUID generation is optional; fallback mechanism is deterministic but non-standard.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When `crypto.randomUUID` is undefined, intent-id falls back to `ci_<base36>_<base36>`

layer2.mapping: Client intent-id generation is isomorphic to server-side validation logic under constraint of UUID availability.
layer2.telemetry: Observed via test suite failure when `isValidClientIntentId` is applied to fallback strings.

primitives.name: Receipt Integrity Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Live anonymous `/picks` renders, on the free card: *"This pick was frozen into a SHA-256 receipt before kickoff.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H': 'SHA-256 hash output (dimensionless)', 't': 'time of freeze (seconds since epoch)'}
primitives.assumptions: Pick data is immutable post-freeze; SHA-256 collision resistance holds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t < kickoff time, H is valid; otherwise, H is invalid.

layer2.mapping: The SHA-256 hash function acts as a cryptographic isomorphism between pick data and its integrity signature, preserving semantic meaning under transformation.

primitives.name: Model Signal Commitment
primitives.verbatim_quote: on-pipeline/src/process-sport.ts:846-853` skips the mint when `entryOdds === 0`, so model-signal moneylines publish uncommitted.
primitives.assumptions: Commitment occurs iff O ≠ 0; m is derived from stochastic process.
primitives.breakdown_regime: C = true iff O ≠ 0; otherwise C = false.

layer2.mapping: Commitment kernel is defined by conditional probability P(C|O≠0) = 1, implying deterministic commitment logic.

primitives.name: Promotion Geo Isolation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Also verified as **latent, not live**: the `/promotions` geo gap.
primitives.assumptions: Geo isolation implies L > 0; S = false when options.state is null.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If S = false, then G is ignored; else, G is enforced.

layer2.mapping: Latent state enforcement is modeled as a Boolean kernel K(S,G) = ¬S ∨ G, where latent behavior is active when S is false.

primitives.name: Checkout Consent Defect
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Never write universal "every pick is sealed with a receipt before kickoff" copy** — not as tagline, hero, or paywall text.
primitives.assumptions: Auto-initiation violates explicit consent; P = true iff U ∧ C.
primitives.breakdown_regime: P = true only when both U and C are true.

layer2.mapping: Consent kernel K(U,C) = U ∧ C defines valid payment initiation; failure to enforce leads to policy violation.
layer2.telemetry: Payment initiation events vs. explicit consent flags

primitives.name: Verifiability Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: The skeptics who respond to verifiability are precisely the people who enumerate endpoints and diff pages.
primitives.assumptions: User skepticism increases inversely with system verifiability; verifiability is a function of endpoint and page consistency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When V < threshold, user trust collapses due to inconsistency between stated and actual behavior.

layer2.mapping: Verifiability constraint maps to a Bayesian posterior over system truth, where inconsistency implies high entropy in belief update.
layer2.telemetry: User feedback loops on endpoint discrepancies and page diffs

primitives.name: Trust Anchor
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is a product decision that determines whether the coverage gap is fixed by minting more or by publishing less.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'Trust anchor strength (dimensionless)', 'C': 'Coverage gap (count)', 'M': 'Minted content units (count)', 'P': 'Published content units (count)'}
primitives.assumptions: Trust is anchored by content consistency; increasing M without reducing P leads to dilution of T.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C > 0 and P < M, trust degrades due to perceived overproduction without quality control.

layer2.mapping: Trust anchor is derived from the ratio of published to minted content under a quality constraint, forming a kernel of product integrity.
layer2.telemetry: Content-to-mint ratio and user retention post-publish

primitives.assumptions: Pitch strength is a composite of volume, confidence, and audience alignment; weaker pitches reduce conversion probability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S < threshold, pitch fails to convert users due to insufficient persuasive signal.
